title: KOD-75-AC-3 — A lane is READY iff it is approved and every in-scope blocker's subtree is Done; a blocked lane never dispatches
description:
**Check:** A lane is READY iff it is approved and every in-scope blocker issue's subtree is Done; the ready set recomputes as lanes reach Done, and a blocked lane never dispatches.
**Do:** Implement the READY predicate in `chains/scope_walker.py` over live tracker state: `scope:approved` self-or-ancestor, plus blocker-subtree-Done read as a rollup over children. Fixture: a blocked lane held across ticks, then admitted as its blocker's subtree completes.
**Evidence:** 138958c — tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py::test_a_blocked_lane_is_held_across_ticks_until_its_blockers_subtree_closes, ::test_a_done_blocker_parent_with_an_open_criterion_still_blocks_its_lane, ::test_the_gated_pass_runs_the_scope_dispatcher_and_follows_the_fire, ::test_a_scope_with_no_ready_lane_enqueues_nothing_and_reports_empty, ::test_ready_selection_makes_no_writes_before_the_claim, tests/services/test_fire_dispatcher.py, tests/services/test_dispatch_pass.py, tests/tracker/test_tracker_boot_wiring.py pass; revert-check: reverting the blocked-lane exclusion list in services/scope_dispatcher.py::run_pass reds test_a_blocked_lane_is_held_across_ticks_until_its_blockers_subtree_closes and test_a_done_blocker_parent_with_an_open_criterion_still_blocks_its_lane; gate 9058 passed/17 skipped at 138958c; judged 2026-09-08 (workhorse tier, provisional): REFUTED — the Check clause 'a blocked lane never dispatches' is demonstrated only inside the test module's own hand-built wiring: grep -rn ScopeDispatcher src/ finds it in no production file other than src/kodezart/services/scope_dispatcher.py itself, so no shipped caller exercises the blocked-lane hold and the clause the 2026-09-08 audit named stays open. The rest does hold: reverting 138958c deletes src/kodezart/services/scope_dispatcher.py and reds the cited scope suite (ImportError at tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py:16) while the other cited suites are untouched (134 passed), and chains/scope_walker.py:60-90 really does recompute approval plus in-scope-blocker subtree closure from scratch each pass with across-ticks fixtures asserting real effects.

title: KOD-75-AC-18 — Gap membership is total over criterion sub-issue state with no default arm, and an ungraded criterion is never refuted
description:
**Check:** Gap membership is total over criterion sub-issue state with no default arm, one case per state: a criterion moved back from Done is in the gap and ungraded; a criterion never graded is in the gap and ungraded with no graded sha, asserted **not** refuted; a lapse-derived ungraded criterion carries its prior graded sha in its Evidence row, and the two are distinguished by that sha rather than by a fourth state.
**Do:** Compute the gap in the gap domain module from the issue's subtree criteria — not Done and not Canceled-with-supersession — with one arm per state and no `else`. Table test, one row per state.
**Evidence:** 4173669 — tests/chains/test_scope_gap_membership.py::test_the_membership_table_carries_one_arm_per_tracker_state, ::test_one_gap_arm_per_criterion_state_over_the_subtree (one row per WorkflowStateKind member × linear and fake), ::test_a_criterion_moved_back_from_done_is_owed_again_with_its_graded_sha, ::test_a_criterion_never_graded_is_owed_with_no_graded_sha_and_not_refuted, ::test_the_two_ungraded_readings_are_told_apart_by_the_sha_alone pass; gate 9235/25; judged 2026-09-09 (workhorse tier): REFUTED — measured, not inferred. The Check is about gap MEMBERSHIP, but 3 of the cited table's 7 rows are decided by a barrier upstream of the gap module: BACKLOG raises `ScopePlanRefusalError` in `src/kodezart/services/scope_planning.py` before any gap is computed, and CANCELED and DUPLICATE raise `ScopeSupersessionReadError` in `src/kodezart/domain/issue_tree.py::open_criteria`, which refuses on state alone and passes `supersession_refs={}`, so `compute_gap` is never reached for them. Proof: I gutted the production predicate's three arms in `src/kodezart/domain/gap.py` (BACKLOG/CANCELED/DUPLICATE → False, i.e. a cancellation with no supersession is discharged — precisely the defect the rule exists to forbid) and re-ran the whole cited file: 21/21 still passed, fully green; only the uncited pre-existing `tests/domain/test_gap.py` caught it (5 failures). So the evidence pins membership for 4 states (triage/unstarted/started/completed) and, for the other 3, pins a refusal the criterion does not own; the only half of the rule that excludes anything beyond Done — Canceled-WITH-supersession — is unreachable on the path the table measures.

title: KOD-75-AC-15 — Plan-time refusal holds the walk, and every fire re-validates its Todo criterion sub-issues at head before the loop
description:
**Check:** Stage barriers: the plan-time refusal scans each member's subtree, so an approved scope containing an issue whose subtree holds an open `decision` or a Backlog criterion sub-issue never begins the walk, and the refusal names the offending keys wherever they sit; every fire is execution-only and re-validates its subtree's Todo criterion sub-issues at head before it reaches the ralph loop. The fire graph holds no ticket- or criteria-generation node.
**Do:** Add the plan-time refusal to the planner and a pre-loop re-validation step to the fire graph that lists the issue's subtree criteria. Fixtures: a refused scope that dispatches nothing; a refused scope whose only offending key sits under a deliverable child; a fire whose pre-loop step runs before the loop node; a static assertion that no generation node exists.
**Evidence:** c906cbb on `kodezart/v03-r1-02` (clauses 2-3; clause 1 stands at f1951f3, now on trunk) — tests/chains/test_native_fire.py::test_the_native_fire_graph_holds_no_ticket_or_criteria_generation_node, ::test_the_loop_is_unreachable_without_the_pre_loop_step, ::test_a_criterion_that_lost_its_check_stops_the_fire_before_the_loop, ::test_the_criteria_a_fire_owes_are_its_subtrees_todo_criteria, ::test_a_criterion_the_fire_does_not_owe_is_not_revalidated, ::test_an_unwired_deployment_composes_no_native_arm_at_all, ::test_an_unwired_engine_still_refuses_an_addressed_run, ::test_a_container_address_is_not_a_fire, ::test_the_addressed_issue_is_the_subject_the_run_carries pass; gate 9202 passed/25 skipped; judged 2026-09-09 (workhorse tier): REFUTED — ran all 13 tests in tests/chains/test_native_fire.py at 7a7185e (13 passed), then drove the case the Check DESCRIBES rather than the one it forbids: a native fire whose criteria all state a Check, through `fire.run(scope=ScopeRef(ISSUE, 'fire/subject'))`. It never reaches the loop. The barrier passes (log: fire_criteria_read named=3 owed=['fire/owed-direct','fire/owed-direct-2','fire/owed-nested']) and then run_ralph_loop dies: RuntimeError: The ticket is read after generation; state['ticket'] is None — at src/kodezart/chains/fire_implementation.py:128 -> src/kodezart/domain/workflow_state.py:46. Cause: `TrackerCriteria.revalidate_criteria` returns {} ([criteria.py:105](<http://criteria.py:105>)), so on the native arm state['ticket'] and state['criteria_artifact'] both stay None and the very next node reads both through current_ticket/validated_criteria. The clause 'every fire … re-validates its subtree's Todo criterion sub-issues at head BEFORE IT REACHES THE RALPH LOOP' is therefore vacuous on this arm: nothing can reach the loop, so the step precedes an unreachable node. The claim says the ordering is proved at runtime, but the only runtime drive test (`test_a_criterion_that_lost_its_check_stops_the_fire_before_the_loop`) is a REFUSAL case asserting gate.calls == []; grepping native_graph/revalidate_criteria found no happy-path drive of the native arm in any other test file.

title: KOD-75-AC-5 — Anti-deadlock: a scope of open unmerged PRs still walks to completion, and a blocker Done with no PR unlocks identically
description:
**Check:** Anti-deadlock: a scope in which every lane's PR is opened and left open and unmerged still walks the entire graph to completion, and a blocker Done with **no PR at all** unlocks its dependent identically.
**Do:** Keep the ready set a function of blocker Done alone, with no landing or merge precondition. Two fixtures over the fake forge: all-PRs-open-and-unmerged walks to completion; a Done blocker with no PR admits its dependent on the same tick.
**Evidence:** 3ea6fde — tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py::test_a_scope_of_open_unmerged_pull_requests_walks_to_completion, ::test_a_blocker_done_with_no_pull_request_unlocks_on_the_same_tick, ::test_an_open_criterion_holds_a_dependent_whatever_its_refs_say pass; revert-check: substituting a recorded-deliverable-ref rule for the subtree-closure blocking rule in chains/scope_walker.py::read_scope_ready reds test_an_open_criterion_holds_a_dependent_whatever_its_refs_say; gate 9067 passed/17 skipped at 3ea6fde. Brief-named tests one and two exceeded the 88-column ruff limit as identifiers and ship shortened, same assertions.; judged 2026-09-08 (workhorse tier, provisional): REFUTED — the Check's first clause holds only under the fixture's ordering. walk_chain at tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py:229-249 opens each lane's delivery only AFTER that lane has been dispatched and its criterion closed, so an open delivery is never presented to a candidate. Re-run of the same three-lane chain with the deliveries already open at tick zero — walk(tracker, delivered=('A','B','C')) — enqueues nothing on the first pass: outcome=empty_eligible_set, exclusions [('A', OPEN_DELIVERY), ('B', LIVE_BLOCKER), ('C', LIVE_BLOCKER)], enqueued=[]. So 'a scope in which every lane's PR is opened and left open and unmerged still walks the entire graph to completion' is false; the open-delivery precondition the walker still asks (services/scope_dispatcher.py:91 -> fire_dispatcher.py:673 _delivery_exclusion) sits on the dispatch path, against the Do's 'no landing precondition'.

title: KOD-75-AC-13 — Degeneration: a single issue with no in-scope blockers runs identically to today's single fire

Measured side by side on the same board with an ordinary single issue and no criterion child: the unscoped producer reports fire_enqueued and enqueues ['K-2'], while the scoped walker RAISES EmptyFireCriteriaError (fire subject has no criterion sub-issues) from src/kodezart/domain/issue_tree.py:80, reached via chains/scope_walker.py:68 open_criteria(closure.criteria(key)). That is the defect the audit named — single-issue scoped input raising rather than degenerating through the authored fire path — still standing, with no decision comment scoping it out, so 'runs identically to today's single fire' fails. Secondary: the Do's 'node sequence' is never compared.

title: KOD-75-AC-16 — The dispatch target is the issue itself; no marker is resolved and no description text is read to find it
description:
**Check:** Dispatch resolution is by tracker identity alone: the dispatch target IS the issue, so a container holding two members with no parent inside it resolves unambiguously; an issue outside the approved scope is refused at plan time rather than reaching the walk; the walker records no read of description text when resolving a dispatch target. Lane markers are dropped.
**Do:** Resolve dispatch targets from issue keys and the `scope:approved` self-or-ancestor cascade; no marker lookup and no prose parsing anywhere in the walker. Fixtures: the two-member container; an out-of-scope issue refused; the fake tracker's description-read counter asserted zero.
**Evidence:** 8257113 — tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py::test_a_container_of_two_root_members_resolves_the_dispatch_target_by_key, ::test_an_unapproved_member_never_reaches_the_walk, ::test_dispatch_target_resolution_reads_no_description_text, ::test_walker_modules_resolve_no_lane_marker_and_parse_no_prose pass; revert-check: replacing the execution_approved read in chains/scope_walker.py::read_scope_ready with an unconditional True reds test_an_unapproved_member_never_reaches_the_walk; gate 9072 passed/17 skipped at 8257113; judged 2026-09-08 (workhorse tier, provisional): REFUTED — the Check clause 'an issue outside the approved scope is refused at plan time rather than reaching the walk' is unmet on both halves. Not at plan time: read_scope_plan explicitly establishes no approval (src/kodezart/services/scope_planning.py:12-17), so the unapproved member is read into the plan and its subtree read, and approval is first consulted INSIDE the walk at chains/scope_walker.py:66. Not refused: running the shipped two_roots fixture with only the first root approved gives report.exclusions == [] for the second — silently dropped, with no refusal, no exclusion clause and no log; and a wholly unapproved scope (approved=()) returns outcome=empty_eligible_set, eligible=(), exclusions=(), enqueued=[], byte-identical to the report for a scope at rest, so 'not approved' is indistinguishable from 'nothing ready'.

title: KOD-75-AC-6 — The ready-set computation makes zero reads of PR merge state; the fake forge's merge-state reader records no calls
description:
**Check:** The ready-set computation makes zero reads of PR merge state; the fake forge's merge-state reader records no calls.
**Do:** Keep merge state out of the ready-set code path entirely. The fake forge counts calls to its merge-state reader; assert zero across a full walk, and assert the ready-set module holds no call site for it.

The companion static test at :408-434 scans a module list only and does not cover the walk, so the clause is satisfied solely by the test's own fixture.; reproduced 2026-09-08 (a walk monkeypatched to read merge state on every delivery check left the shipped `assert reader.calls == []` green), then repaired 5da3869 — the forge double now answers DeliveryProbe and PRStateReader from one object, as the native client does, so the probe the walk is already handed IS the merge-state reader; tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py::test_a_full_walk_reads_no_pull_request_merge_state asserts the forge was asked about all three lanes' deliveries (`set(probe.calls) == {A,B,C}`) and asked nothing about their pull requests (`probe.merge_state.calls == []`). The static half no longer names modules from memory: ::test_no_module_the_walk_can_reach_holds_a_merge_state_call_site computes the walk's import closure (68 modules from services/scope_dispatcher outwards) and forbids a held PRStateReader or a read_pr_state call site anywhere on it. Both pass, with ::test_ready_set_and_walker_modules_hold_no_merge_state_call_site unchanged; mutation-checks: reading merge state through the forge inside FireDispatcher._delivery_exclusion reds the walk fixture, and importing PRStateReader into services/fire_dispatcher.py reds the closure test; gate 9075 passed/17 skipped at 5da3869; re-judged 2026-09-08 by graphcode-46 (workhorse tier, provisional): the original counterexample now holds; three refuters — contract, test-strength, revert — none refuted. Provisional pending top-tier re-verification.

title: KOD-75-AC-26 — GapMeasurement is absent from every durable surface the run writes and present on the point-in-time surface

title: KOD-75-AC-33 — Walker settings express operator choices; stable constants stay in code
description:
**Check:** Operator-adjustable walk cadence and plateau policy are read from their subsystem settings and a non-default value changes the composed walker's behavior. A new setting requires an identified production consumer and a concrete deployment variation; stable algorithm constants and provider grammars may live in code at their owning boundary. The provided-capability set is derived from the composed implementation unless an operator choice is demonstrated. No blanket numeric-literal ban or test requiring every number to become configuration remains.

**Do:** Replace the no-literal doctrine with consumer-owned settings and explicit policy. Remove unused knobs or wire a setting only when the active behavior requires it; do not keep fields solely to satisfy this criterion. Test observable override behavior at the composed consumer, not the presence of a field or the absence of literals.

**Evidence:** Pending verification of the amended contract.

**Plan amendment · 2026-09-08:** Supersedes this criterion's requirement that every numeric knob become a `KODEZART_` `AppConfig` field. [KOD-744](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744>) owns the simplification plan; historical comments apply to the previous contract.

title: KOD-75-AC-21 — A lane whose gap is empty is not dispatched whatever its state field says; the paired ungraded lane is dispatched
description:
**Check:** A lane whose subtree is closed — its own `criterion` sub-issues and its deliverable children's subtrees, recursively — is not dispatched whatever its own workflow state field says, and the dispatch decision records no read of that field; the paired lane whose field says Done while one criterion sub-issue is still ungraded **is** dispatched, carrying exactly that criterion; a third lane whose own criteria are all Done while one criterion is open under a child deliverable is not treated as finished, and its dispatch decision is recorded rather than silent.
**Do:** Key the dispatch decision on the gap alone, never on the parent's state field. Three fixtures over the fake tracker; assert the parent-state field reader records zero calls in the dispatch path, that the dispatched fire carries exactly the ungraded criterion, and that the open-under-a-child-deliverable lane is neither treated as finished nor left without a recorded decision.
**Evidence:** — (sha · met-gap and paired-ungraded test names · session id)

title: KOD-75-AC-4 — Crashed-lane re-eligibility: an open-PR lane is excluded as delivered-in-review, a no-PR no-run lane stays eligible
description:
**Check:** Crashed-lane re-eligibility holds: a lane whose PR is open is excluded as delivered-in-review; a lane with no PR and no live run is still eligible.
**Do:** Re-entry eligibility asks the forge for an open PR and the run store for a live run, and reads neither merge state nor a body. Two fixtures over the fake forge: open-PR lane excluded, no-PR/no-run lane admitted.
**Evidence:** 29c1683 — tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py::test_a_lane_with_an_open_pull_request_is_excluded_as_delivered_in_review, ::test_a_lane_with_a_live_run_is_excluded_as_in_flight, ::test_a_lane_with_no_pull_request_and_no_live_run_is_eligible, ::test_re_entry_eligibility_reads_no_merge_state_and_no_body pass; revert-check: dropping the delivery clause from FireDispatcher.standing_exclusion reds test_a_lane_with_an_open_pull_request_is_excluded_as_delivered_in_review and test_re_entry_eligibility_reads_no_merge_state_and_no_body; gate 9064 passed/17 skipped at 29c1683; judged 2026-09-08 (workhorse tier, provisional): REFUTED — the test cited for the negative half is half-vacuous. tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py:503 constructs reader = FakePRStateReader(records={}) that is never passed to walk() (signature at :152 accepts no reader) nor to any object under test, so assert reader.calls == [] at :517 asserts a constant — 'reads no merge state' is established by an unconnected double. The body half is narrower than its name: the monkeypatched `__getattribute__` at :507-511 trips only for issue_key == 'crashed', proving nothing about the eligible lane's body. The cited sha 29c1683 is test-only (1 file, +89/-1), so its revert-check deletes tests rather than production code. Both Check clauses are genuinely implemented and load-bearing in shipped code (mutating FireDispatcher.standing_exclusion reds the positive fixtures); it is the evidence for the negative half that does not hold.; reproduced 2026-09-08 (a pass monkeypatched to read merge state on a reader AND to read the eligible lane's body left both shipped assertions green), then repaired 75ea15e — the forge double answers DeliveryProbe and PRStateReader from one object as the native client does, so the probe the pass is handed IS the merge-state reader, and the description hook now stands over every issue the pass touches and is lifted at launch (what a fire reads once it owns a lane is the fire's business). tests/services/test_scope_dispatcher.py::test_re_entry_eligibility_reads_no_merge_state_and_no_body now asserts body_reads == [], probe.calls == ['crashed', 'fresh'], probe.merge_state.calls == [], the eligible lane claimed and enqueued; ::test_a_lane_with_an_open_pull_request_is_excluded_as_delivered_in_review, ::test_a_lane_with_a_live_run_is_excluded_as_in_flight, ::test_a_lane_with_no_pull_request_and_no_live_run_is_eligible unchanged and pass; mutation-checks: reading merge state through the forge, or reading the eligible lane's body, inside FireDispatcher.standing_exclusion each reds it; gate 9075 passed/17 skipped at 75ea15e; re-judged 2026-09-08 by graphcode-46 (workhorse tier, provisional): the original counterexample now holds; three refuters — contract, test-strength, revert — none refuted. Provisional pending top-tier re-verification.

title: KOD-75-AC-25 — With the plateau bound at 1, a tick closing no open criterion ends the fire with a PR from its best iteration
description:
**Check:** With the plateau bound at 1, a tick that closes **no previously-open criterion sub-issue in the fire's subtree** ends the fire on plateau: a PR is opened from the best iteration, the issue goes back to Todo with that PR as its work ref, the walk continues rather than halting, and the issue is re-dispatched only on a re-entry event. A tick closing twelve criterion references while surfacing twelve new ones (in-gap cardinality flat) is asserted **not** a plateau, a tick whose gap grows through a lapse is asserted **not** a plateau, and a tick whose only closure is a criterion under a deliverable child — no own criterion sub-issue closed — is asserted **not** a plateau.
**Do:** Track the set of previously-open subtree criterion keys per tick, not the gap's size. On plateau or budget exhaustion, open the PR from the best iteration and write the issue back to Todo with the PR as work ref. Four fixtures: plateau, flat-cardinality churn, lapse growth, descendant-only closure.
**Evidence:** — (sha · plateau test names · session id)

title: KOD-75-AC-20 — Over a table of lane fixtures a lane's gap is empty iff the fire-state arithmetic returns Done
description:
**Check:** Over a table of lane fixtures a lane's gap is empty **iff** the subtree rollup returns Done. One arithmetic: an issue's subtree is its own `criterion` children plus its deliverable children's subtrees, recursively, and that single read answers both what a fire still owes and whether a blocker is discharged. A lane with every criterion passing and one non-compliant ruling mark, and a lane with every child Done and one unsatisfied lane check, both hold a non-empty gap and are not Done — rulings land on the affected criterion and lane checks are themselves criterion sub-issues, so in both fixtures the offending criterion is simply not Done. An implementation whose gap ranges over a narrower set than the issue's subtree criteria fails — in particular the met-lane-check-over-an-open-child-deliverable fixture.
**Do:** Compute Done through `SubtreeClosure.is_closed` over the issue's subtree and assert gap-emptiness and Done agree row by row against it. Delete the test-local `fire_state_is_done` restatement at tests/domain/test_subtree_closure.py:102-114 so the iff is read against an arithmetic defined independently of the gap. Every expected value on every row — the open-key tuple and the Done verdict — is authored as a literal on that parametrize row, never recomputed from the function under test, so a row can fail. Table test carrying all five fixtures, the met lane check over an open child deliverable among them as the discriminating row.
**Evidence:** b98d53e — tests/domain/test_subtree_closure.py::test_gap_is_empty_iff_the_subtree_rollup_is_done (all five rows, both expectations authored as literals), ::test_the_lane_gap_and_the_blocker_closure_are_one_read, ::test_a_closure_over_a_narrower_criterion_set_disagrees_with_the_gap, ::test_issue_tree_module_imports_no_adapters_and_does_no_io, tests/chains/test_scope_ready.py::test_a_graded_lane_over_an_out_of_filter_open_child_is_not_at_rest, ::test_deliverable_grandchildren_outside_membership_are_owed_and_dispatched pass; gate 9077 passed/17 skipped at b98d53e. One arithmetic shipped at f5b17f2: the subtree closure's `gap` returns every still-open criterion record under a key and is_closed is its emptiness, so the walker's candidate gap and its blocker closure are the same read; the test-local fire_state_is_done restatement is deleted. Revert-checks: restoring the narrow candidate read at chains/scope_walker.py (open_criteria(closure.criteria(key))) reds both named scope-ready tests, the loss shape returning ready == [] instead of the lane owing its child's check; defining is_closed as `not open_criteria(self.criteria(key), ref=self.ref)` reds the discriminating row [a_met_lane_check_over_an_open_child_deliverable] and ::test_the_lane_gap_and_the_blocker_closure_are_one_read.

title: KOD-75-AC-1 — The planner enumerates the ready set over a fixture blockedBy graph and ranks it by effective priority then age
description:
**Check:** The topology planner, over a fixture `blockedBy` graph, enumerates the scope's ready set — the issues with no open blocker — and ranks it for a deep stack: effective priority (the max of its own and of everything it transitively blocks) first, then age, oldest first. Lane order, per-scope concurrency and lane caps are not computed; the walk dispatches one fire per pass.
**Do:** Build the planner over `blockedBy` edges in `src/kodezart/domain/topology.py`: the open-blocker predicate, cycle detection, and the effective-priority-then-age rank. Fixture graph with parallel roots and a deep stack; assert the ready set and the rank order.
**Evidence:** — (sha · planner fixture test names · session id)
